question: Should OpenClaw standardize these three host-neutral recovery lifecycle sidecars above RFC 0013, or keep aggregate handoff and restored-admission semantics outside the RFC set for now?
rationale: The patch is a new cross-boundary contract, not a correction to an established behavior; source review cannot determine whether OpenClaw should own these lifecycle guarantees or their compatibility commitment.

options.title: Accept the sidecar boundary
options.body: Adopt the narrowly scoped recovery-point, host-handoff, and restored-admission contracts while retaining the stated host-owned responsibilities.

options.title: Narrow the RFC further
options.body: Keep only the portions needed to document current owner primitives and defer aggregate handoff or restored-admission semantics until their implementation direction is settled.

options.title: Defer lifecycle standardization
options.body: Leave RFC 0013 as the SQLite artifact contract and move the proposed lifecycle semantics to implementation-specific or external-host documentation for now.

recommendation.title: Accept the sidecar boundary
recommendation.body: Adopt the narrowly scoped recovery-point, host-handoff, and restored-admission contracts while retaining the stated host-owned responsibilities.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and discussion connect Vincent to the shipped SQLite snapshot boundary whose scope this addendum would extend.
